texts: The Cliff Path runs along the outer edge of the village.
The Cliff Path runs from the harbor wall to the cliff-spires.
The cliff-spires stand east of the village.
Flat sea-worn stones pave the Cliff Path.
Each Keeper walks the Cliff Path every night.
The Cliff Path holds one hundred and twelve lanterns.
The middle stretch of the Cliff Path is unshielded.

fields.sentence: The Cliff Path runs along the outer edge of the village.

q2_gaps: extent / course verb of a linear thing ('the path runs along X', 'the road follows the river'): the bare-position route names only lie / sit / stand / hang / lean / perch / rest, so whether 'runs along' mints an event or takes the entity-attached position atom is undetermined

a relational part-noun of a place ('the outer edge of the village'): the genitive part/component test points to PartOf while the 'a place inside a place is LocatedIn, never PartOf' geography rule points to LocatedIn, and the relational-noun parenthetical ('a tributary of the river') does not settle which side an edge-of-a-place falls on
review.notes: Name/type split, outer_edge decomposition (positional modifier exposed), and the entity-attached (Along ...) head all follow the instruction set; no tense atom is correct for a present-tense position clause.

fields.sentence: The Cliff Path runs from the harbor wall to the cliff-spires.

q2_gaps: verb of spatial extent ('the Cliff Path runs from A to B') — 'run' is not among the stative locative/postural verbs the instruction set lists (lie/sit/stand/hang/lean/perch/rest), so whether such a clause mints an event is left undetermined
a from-to endpoint PAIR naming a linear thing's two termini — entity-attached 'From' is defined only as ORIGIN ('where the wool is from, not where it is'), and no head covers a route's extent
review.notes: Under the position-clause route ('a bare position clause mints no event whatever its verb') the surface verb 'runs' disappears entirely, exactly as 'leaned' does in the instruction set's own (Against ...) example; the definite/plural NP handling (typed witness, group witness, head genus without the noun-modifier genus) all follows the compound rules.

fields.sentence: The cliff-spires stand east of the village.

review.notes: Bare position clause with postural 'stand' correctly mints no event; 'east of' is the entity-attached multi-word surface preposition, present tense correctly unwrapped. Definite plural takes a group witness and the noun-modifier 'cliff' is correctly left unexposed while the genus 'spire' is emitted.

fields.sentence: Flat sea-worn stones pave the Cliff Path.
parse: (: stones_pave_path (Implication (And (Member $x stone) (Member $x flat) (Member $x sea_worn)) (And (Member (sk_pave $x) pave) (Agent (sk_pave $x) $x) (Patient (sk_pave $x) cliff_path))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The bare plural here names the specific set of stones paving that one path, not a generic kind, so the distributing-rule route wrongly asserts that every flat sea-worn stone in the KB paves the Cliff Path; the clause is neither habitual nor a characteristic claim about stones, so the licensed route is a group witness acting in one pave event with the modifiers distributed over its members.

review.notes: The name handling is right: one opaque symbol for "the Cliff Path", its Name atom, and the kind atom read off the kind word inside the name. The episodic-bare-plural test is stated with past/dated/one-off exemplars so a present-tense standing-configuration clause sits at its edge, but the rule route's own precondition (a genuinely generic clause) is not met.

issues.reason: The rule ranges over every flat sea-worn stone in the KB and hands each one a pave event whose Patient is the constant cliff_path, asserting far more than the text states (Core patterns: assert only what the text states) — the sentence describes the specific set of stones surfacing that one named path, not a characteristic claim about stones at large.

new_gaps: The episodic-vs-generic bare-plural test is stated with past/dated/one-off exemplars on the episodic side and habitual-present/characteristic on the generic side; a present-tense STANDING-CONFIGURATION clause ('stones pave the path', 'ivy covers the wall') is neither, and nothing tells the parser which route it takes.
adjudication.defect_summary: Compliant form: a group witness for the specific stones — (GroupOf sk_group_1 stone) with the descriptive modifiers distributed over its members, (Implication (PartOf $x sk_group_1) (Member $x flat)) and the same for sea_worn — filling the Agent of one pave event whose Patient is cliff_path, instead of an Implication ranging over the kind.
adjudication.notes: The name handling is correct: one opaque symbol for the multi-word name, one Name atom, and the kind atom read off the kind word inside the name.

fields.sentence: Each Keeper walks the Cliff Path every night.
parse: (: keeper_walk_rule (Implication (Member $x keeper) (And (Member (sk_walk $x) walk) (Agent (sk_walk $x) $x) (Theme (sk_walk $x) cliff_path) (Time (sk_walk $x) night) (Every (sk_walk $x) 1 day))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

review.notes: The "each" universal takes the distributing rule over (Member $x keeper) with its QuantifierPhrase companion and no tense atom (habitual), and "every night" correctly becomes the day-part Time slot plus the implied (Every e 1 day) cycle. "the Cliff Path" is one opaque name symbol with its kind atom and no modifier genus, per Names and casing.

fields.sentence: The Cliff Path holds one hundred and twelve lanterns.

review.notes: Multi-word name plus in-name kind atom, Agent on the stative transitive (cf. "the tank holds forty litres"), Theme for the unchanged object, and group + Cardinality 112 for the counted plural all follow the instruction set. Only nit: the group symbol is sk_lantern_1 where the stated default is sk_group_1 (a mnemonic stem is licensed "with several groups in play"), which is nominal rather than semantic.

fields.sentence: The middle stretch of the Cliff Path is unshielded.

review.notes: Multi-word name handled per Names and casing (one opaque symbol + one Name + the kind word from inside the name); the of-phrase takes PartOf on the part test, and the positional modifier genus follows the east_wing/upper_deck carve-out. "unshielded" correctly stays a positive property at strength 1.0 (lexical antonyms are not negation).
